sector_verbatim.evidence_quote:
This study reports on 
an electrical energy management system for improving cement plant productivity at minimal 
cost.

country_region.evidence_quote: The energy management system was implemented on a South African cement plant.

scale_of_application.evidence_quote: The energy management system was implemented on a South African cement plant.

scope_description.value: One South African cement plant with a coal-consuming kiln, coal mill, raw mill and two finishing mills; total production capacity almost 1 million tonnes of cement per annum. The study focuses on the electrical portion of energy.
scope_description.evidence_quote:
The case study plant has one coal consuming kiln which is used to produce clinker. The kiln 
has a coal mill, which consumes electrical energy. Furthermore, the plant has a raw mill, and 
two finishing mills, used for producing cement.

reviewer_notes: The paper applies an ISO 50001 based reporting system built on intensity-ratio EnPIs (Equations 1-8). Each distinct EnPI is treated as a separate intensity-ratio model. Two of the defined EnPIs (Clinker production, Total energy per clinker produced) were explicitly not evaluated because the plant does not continuously produce clinker; this is captured as mechanism K1 rather than as separate models. Baseline construction for all EnPIs is the benchmarking on three months' historical performance plus literature values (page 13). No statistical fit or out-of-sample validation applies to intensity ratios; the reported results are energy/cost reductions between the first (Jan-15) and last (Feb-16) implementation months.
